NO. 033 · Wetlands & Waterways / Ardeidae · Herons & Egrets

Eastern Cattle Egret

牛背鹭 · niú bèi lù Bubulcus ibis
Winter visitor / resident Common 46–52 cm Protected (China) IUCN LC

The short-necked white egret that follows the buffalo for insects

It does not belong to the water but to the grass — following cattle, following tractors, picking off the insects they flush. In breeding condition the head, neck and breast flush orange-buff, as if caught in low sunlight.

Gallery

One scientific illustration for shape and colour blocks, two field photographs for how it looks in real light. Click any image to enlarge.

Identification

  • Breeding plumageOrange-buff plumes over crown, neck and breast, with matching orange-buff aigrettes down the centre of the back; warm-toned and very conspicuous.
  • Non-breeding plumageAll white, bill yellow and short, neck short and thick, body thickset — plainly different from the slender Little Egret.
  • NeckMarkedly short and thick, much shorter than in other egrets, and often pulled in so that the bird looks neckless as it stands on grass.
  • BillYellow, short and pointed, made for pecking insects off the ground.

Behaviour

A classic follower: it walks behind cattle, horses and tractors taking insects and frogs they disturb, and also feeds on mown grass and in burnt fields. It nests colonially with other egrets. South China holds both wintering birds and residents; most often seen in farmland and on grassland.

Voice

Usually silent; when alarmed, or at the colony, a short harsh 'rick-rack', dry and unmusical.

Where to find it in Zhuhai

  • Doumen farmland
  • Jinwan grassland
  • Hengqin open ground
  • Qi'ao Island pasture edges
Field note
A white egret on grass with a short neck, a yellow bill and a plump body is this species. The orange-buff plumes of the breeding season make it unmistakable.
